roleContext.jobDescription: The enterprise knowledge base product serves search and document sync to field staff at large customers. The Capacity Planning Analyst forecasts search and sync load per customer, plans index and storage capacity with the platform team, and is expected to reduce capacity-related incidents, reported against the platform's published incident baseline.

requirements.text: Keeps a per-customer forecast of search and sync load and the model behind it.
Turns the forecast into index and storage plans agreed with the platform team.
Reduces capacity-related incidents, reported against the published incident baseline.
Takes capacity changes through the platform and customer teams and records who approved what.
Keeps an assumptions note per planning cycle with limitations and hand-over items.

candidate.originalCvMarkdown:
# Curriculum vitae

Target role: Capacity Planning Analyst, Enterprise Knowledge Base

## Experience

- Kept the per-customer load model that predicts search queries and sync volume from user counts and document growth; every month I recalibrated it against the platform metrics warehouse.
- Turned each quarter's forecast into an index-shard and storage plan that the platform team and I took to the quarterly planning meeting.
- Capacity-related incidents fell from 7 in the first half of the year to 2 in the second half after the shard rebalancing plan was applied, as counted in the platform incident register against its published baseline of 7 incidents per half-year.
- Took capacity changes through the quarterly planning meeting with the platform and customer teams; the platform lead approved shard changes and the customer teams handled communication with their accounts.
- Kept an assumptions note per cycle covering the model inputs, the fact that bulk document imports sat outside the forecast, and what the next cycle inherited.

## Work samples

- Work sample: a year of the incident register filtered to capacity-related incidents (with the baseline and the rebalancing plan marked) and one cycle's assumptions note; export identifiers are included for tracing.
